How to choose a torque wrench range

By Meera Ranganathan, calibration laboratory, published 28 July 2026.

A torque wrench is most accurate in the middle of its range, so the first rule of choosing one is to pick a range whose middle sits near the fasteners you tighten most often. A wrench used constantly at the bottom ten percent of its scale will drift faster and read less consistently than one used near its centre.

Matching range to work

Wheel nuts on passenger cars are usually specified between 100 and 140 newton metres, which sits comfortably in the middle of a 20 to 210 newton metre wrench. Engine covers, sump plugs and small brackets are often below 40 newton metres, which is where a smaller wrench earns its place instead.

How often to recalibrate

Annual recalibration is the common standard, but a wrench that is dropped should be checked immediately regardless of when it was last certified. Keep the certificate with the tool so anyone using it can see the last measured deviation.
